source_text:
σπονδήν. Ὁλοκαυτώματα Σαββάτων ἐν τοῖς Σαββάτοις, ἐπὶ τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διὰ παντὸς, καὶ τὴν σπονδὴν αὐτῆς.» Οὐχ ἕτερος δὲ τῆς θυσίας ὁ τρόπος, παρὰ τὸν ἀρτίως ἡμῖν εἰρημένον. Εἰσὶ δὲ οὗτοι κατ' ἴχνος ὡς παραλλάττειν οὐδέν. Ἄθρει γε μὴν ἐκεῖνο, ὦ τᾶν· ἡ μὲν γὰρ τοῦ ἐνδελεχισμοῦ θυσία διηνεκῆ τὴν ἱερουργίαν ἔχει καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ πάσῃ τελεῖται κατὰ τὸν νόμον. Ἡ δέ γε τῶν Σαββάτων, οὐ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν, ἀλλ' ἐν αὐτοῖς τοῖς Σαββάτοις. Ἵνα τοίνυν μὴ ἀποχρώντως ἔχειν οἰόμενοι τὴν ἀνὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν τοῦ ἐνδελεχισμοῦ θυσίαν, ῥᾴθυμοί πως εἶεν περὶ τὸ προσάγειν τὰ ἐν Σαββάτοις, προστέθεικεν ἀναγκαίως· «Τοῦτό ἐστιν ὁλοκαύτωμα Σαββάτων ἐν τοῖς Σαββάτοις ἐπὶ τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διὰ παντὸς, καὶ τὴν σπονδὴν αὐτῆς.»
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄραρεν οὖν ὅτι πρὸς τῇ θυσίᾳ τοῦ ἐνδελεχισμοῦ, καὶ ἡ τῶν Σαββάτων ἱερουργεῖται κατὰ νόμον;
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἄραρεν· οὐ γὰρ ἐνδοιάσαι θέμις. Σαββατίζοντες γὰρ καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν Χριστῷ, καὶ εἰς τὴν αὐτοῦ κατάπαυσιν εἰσελάσαντες, οἱονεί πως ἐν διπλῷ τὰ τῆς πνευματικῆς εὐωδίας ἀνοίσομεν τῷ Θεῷ, εἴπερ ἐστὶν ἀτρεκὲς, ὡς εὐῶδες μὲν ἦν τοῖς ἀρχαιοτέροις, τῆς ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοσύνης τὸ καύχημα. Πνευματικὸς γὰρ ὁ νόμος, καὶ «Ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία, καὶ δικαία καὶ ἀγαθὴ,» κατὰ τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου φωνήν· ἐν ὑπεροχῇ γε μὴν ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ πολιτεία, καὶ ὁ ἐν πνεύματι σαββατισμὸς, τῆς ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοσύνης ἀμείνων εἰς εὐοσμίαν.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης.
{ΚΥΡ.} Προσεπάγει δὲ τούτοις· «Καὶ ἐν ταῖς νεομηνίαις προσάξετε ὁλοκαύτωμα τῷ Κυρίῳ, μόσχους ἐκ βοῶν δύο, καὶ κριὸν ἕνα· ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους ἑπτὰ ἀμώμους· τρία δέκατα σεμιδάλεως ἀναπεποιημένης ἐν ἐλαίῳ τῷ μόσχῳ τῷ ἑνὶ, καὶ δύο δέκατα σεμιδάλεως ἀναπεποιημένης ἐν ἐλαίῳ τῷ κριῷ τῷ ἑνί· δέκατον δέκατον σεμιδάλεως ἀναπεποιημένης ἐν ἐλαίῳ τῷ ἀμνῷ τῷ ἑνὶ, θυσίαν ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας κάρπωμα Κυρίῳ· ἡ σπονδὴ αὐτῶν τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ ἲν ἔσται τῷ μόσχῳ τῷ ἑνὶ, καὶ τρίτον τοῦ ἳν' ἔσται τῷ κριῷ τῷ ἑνὶ, καὶ τὸ τέταρτον τοῦ ἲν ἔσται τῷ ἀμνῷ τῷ ἑνὶ οἴνου· τοῦτο τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα μῆνα ἐκ μηνὸς εἰς τοὺς μῆνας τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ· καὶ χίμαρον ἐξ αἰγῶν ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας Κυρίῳ· ἐπὶ τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διὰ παντὸς ποιηθήσεται καὶ ἡ σπονδὴ αὐτοῦ.» Διηνεκὴς θυσία καὶ ἀκατάληκτος, ὡς ἂν ἑκάστῳ μηνὶ, πρὸς τῇ καθ' ἡμέραν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐνδελεχισμοῦ, καὶ ἡ ἐν ταῖς νουμηνίαις. Λόγος δὲ οὐχ ἁπλοῦς ὁ ἐπ' αὐταῖς ἔσται πάλιν. Καθαρὸν γὰρ λίαν τὸ αἴνιγμα. Νουμηνία τοίνυν ἡ νοητὴ καὶ ἀληθεστέρα νοοῖτ' ἂν εἰκότως, αἰὼν ὁ νέος ἐν Χριστῷ, παρῳχηκότος τοῦ πρώτου τοῦ κατὰ νόμον. Εἴη δ' ἂν καὶ ἑτέρως εἰς τύπον ἡμῖν ἡ νουμηνία, καὶ τοῦ μετὰ τόνδε μέλλοντος αἰῶνος. καὶ ὅσον οὐδέπω παρεσομένου, πλὴν ἀρχὴν ἔχοντος τὴν ἀνάστασιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι' ἧς εἰς καινότητα μετακεχωρήκαμεν, ὡς ἐν ἀῤῥαβῶνι τῆς χάριτος τὸ Πνεῦμα πλουτήσαντες, καὶ ἀσφαλῆ τὴν ἐλπίδα τῆς εἰς
pass_a_gloss: (and) libation. Whole burnt offerings of Sabbaths on the Sabbaths, besides the whole burnt offering throughout all, and its libation.' And the way of the sacrifice is not other besides the one just now said by us. And these are in its track, so as to differ in nothing. Observe however that thing, my good man; for the sacrifice of continuance has a perpetual sacred service and is performed on every day according to the law. But that of the Sabbaths, not on every day, but on the Sabbaths themselves. So then lest, thinking the sacrifice of continuance throughout every day to hold sufficiently, they should somehow be negligent about bringing the things on Sabbaths, he added necessarily: 'This is the whole burnt offering of Sabbaths on the Sabbaths, besides the whole burnt offering throughout all, and its libation.' PALL.: It is fixed then that in addition to the sacrifice of continuance, that of the Sabbaths also is sacrificed according to law? CYR.: It is fixed; for it is not right to doubt. For we too, keeping Sabbath in Christ and having driven into his rest, will offer up to God as it were in double the things of the spiritual fragrance, if it is true that the boast of the righteousness in the law was fragrant to the more ancient ones. For spiritual is the law, and 'the commandment holy and just and good', according to the voice of the blessed Paul; but in superiority is the citizenship in Christ, and the sabbath-keeping in spirit is better toward fragrance than the righteousness in law. PALL.: You spoke well. CYR.: And he adds to these: 'And in the new moons you will bring a whole burnt offering to the Lord, calves from cattle two, and one ram, lambs a year old seven unblemished; three tenths of fine flour mixed in oil for the one calf, and two tenths of fine flour mixed in oil for the one ram; a tenth, a tenth of fine flour mixed in oil for the one lamb, a sacrifice odor of fragrance, an offering to the Lord; their libation will be the half of the hin for the one calf, and a third of the hin will be for the one ram, and the fourth of the hin will be for the one lamb, of wine; this is the whole burnt offering month from month for the months of the year; and one he-goat from goats concerning sin to the Lord; besides the whole burnt offering throughout all it will be done, and its libation.' A perpetual sacrifice and unceasing, as it were for each month, in addition to the daily one, which is of continuance, also the one in the new moons. And the account about them will not again be simple (single). For very clean (clear) is the riddle. So the spiritual and truer new moon would reasonably be understood as the new age in Christ, the first one, the one according to law, having passed by. And it would also be otherwise a type for us, the new moon, also of the age about to be after this one, and all but present, except having as beginning the resurrection of Christ, through which we have changed over into newness, having been enriched with the Spirit as in a pledge of the grace, and (having) the hope secure of the (life) unto (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …a drink offering. These are the whole burnt offerings of the sabbaths, on the sabbaths, besides the continual whole burnt offering and its drink offering’ (Numbers 28:9–10). The manner of the sacrifice is no different from the one we have just described; these follow it step by step, so as to differ in nothing. But notice this, my friend: the continual sacrifice is a perpetual service and is performed every day according to the law, but that of the sabbaths is not offered every day, only on the sabbaths themselves. So, lest they think the continual sacrifice offered every day enough, and grow somehow careless about bringing the offerings of the sabbaths, he necessarily added, ‘This is the whole burnt offering of the sabbaths on the sabbaths, besides the continual whole burnt offering and its drink offering’ (Numbers 28:10).
Palladius: So it is settled, then, that besides the continual sacrifice the sacrifice of the sabbaths too is offered according to the law?

Cyril: It is settled; it is not right to doubt it. For we too, keeping sabbath in Christ and having entered into his rest (Hebrews 4:10), shall offer to God the things of spiritual fragrance in double measure, as it were, if indeed it is true that the boast of righteousness under the law was fragrant to those of old. For the law is spiritual (Romans 7:14), and ‘the commandment is holy and just and good’ (Romans 7:12), in the words of the blessed Paul; yet the life in Christ stands higher, and the sabbath-keeping in the spirit is better in fragrance than the righteousness under the law.

Cyril: He adds to these: ‘And at the new moons you shall bring a whole burnt offering to the Lord: two calves from the herd, and one ram, seven unblemished lambs a year old; three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for the one calf, and two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for the one ram; a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for each lamb, a sacrifice, a fragrant aroma, an offering to the Lord. Their drink offering shall be half a hin for the one calf, and a third of a hin for the one ram, and a quarter of a hin of wine for the one lamb. This is the whole burnt offering month by month, through the months of the year; and one male goat from the goats for sin to the Lord; it shall be offered besides the continual whole burnt offering, and its drink offering’ (Numbers 28:11–15).

A perpetual and unceasing sacrifice, then, as it were: each month, besides the daily one, which is the continual sacrifice, there is also the one at the new moons. The account of them, again, will not be of one kind only, for the riddle is quite clear. The spiritual and truer new moon may fittingly be understood as the new age in Christ, since the first one, under the law, has passed away. But in another way the new moon would also be for us a type of the age that is to come after this one and is all but here, though it has its beginning in the resurrection of Christ. Through it we have passed over into newness, enriched with the Spirit as the pledge of grace (2 Corinthians 1:22), and holding a sure hope of the life that leads to…

choices.term: Λόγος δὲ οὐχ ἁπλοῦς ὁ ἐπ' αὐταῖς ἔσται πάλιν. Καθαρὸν γὰρ λίαν τὸ αἴνιγμα.
choices.english: The account of them, again, will not be of one kind only, for the riddle is quite clear.
choices.why: ἁπλοῦς as 'single': Cyril goes on to give two readings (the present new age; the age to come).
Double offering on sabbaths answers to the double fragrance of law-righteousness and life in Christ.
